        self._register(f"{p}:ENABLE", lambda cmd, s=ii: self._i2c_enable(cmd, s))
        self._register(f"{p}:WRITE", lambda cmd, s=ii: self._i2c_write(cmd, s))
        self._register(f"{p}:READ", lambda cmd, s=ii: self._i2c_read(cmd, s))
        self._register(f"{p}:TRANSFER", lambda cmd, s=ii: self._i2c_transfer(cmd, s))

    def _i2c_addr(self, cmd: ScpiCommand, ii: I2CState) -> str:
        if cmd.is_query:
            return f"0x{ii.address:02X}"
        if cmd.params:
            ii.address = int(cmd.params[0], 0) & 0x7F
        return ""

    def _i2c_freq(self, cmd: ScpiCommand, ii: I2CState) -> str:
        if cmd.is_query:
            return str(ii.clock_frequency)
        if cmd.params:
            v = int(cmd.params[0])
            if v not in (100000, 400000, 1000000):
                pass  # Accept non-standard frequencies
            ii.clock_frequency = v
        return ""

    def _i2c_master(self, cmd: ScpiCommand, ii: I2CState) -> str:
        if cmd.is_query:
            return "1" if ii.master else "0"
        if cmd.params:
            ii.master = cmd.params[0].upper() in ("1", "ON", "MASTER")
        return ""

    def _i2c_enable(self, cmd: ScpiCommand, ii: I2CState) -> str:
        if cmd.is_query:
            return "1" if ii.enabled else "0"
        if cmd.params:
            ii.enabled = cmd.params[0].upper() in ("1", "ON")
        return ""

    def _i2c_write(self, cmd: ScpiCommand, ii: I2CState) -> str:
        if cmd.params:
            data_hex = cmd.params[0].strip('"\'')
            try:
                data = bytes.fromhex(data_hex)
                ii.tx_buffer.extend(data)
            except ValueError:
                raise ScpiError(-151, "Invalid hex string")
        return "ACK"

    def _i2c_read(self, cmd: ScpiCommand, ii: I2CState) -> str:
        n = int(cmd.params[0]) if cmd.params else 1
        data = bytes(ii.rx_buffer[:n])
        ii.rx_buffer = ii.rx_buffer[n:]
        return data.hex() if data else ("00" * n)

    def _i2c_transfer(self, cmd: ScpiCommand, ii: I2CState) -> str:
        if len(cmd.params) >= 2:
            addr = int(cmd.params[0], 0)
            data_hex = cmd.params[1].strip('"\'')
            try:
                data = bytes.fromhex(data_hex)
                ii.tx_buffer.extend(data)
                response = bytes(ii.rx_buffer[:len(data)])
                ii.rx_buffer = ii.rx_buffer[len(data):]
                return response.hex() if response else ("00" * len(data))
            except ValueError:
                raise ScpiError(-151, "Invalid hex string")
        return ""

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # CPU handlers
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _cpu_reset(self, cmd: ScpiCommand) -> str:
        self._running = False
        self._halted = False
        self._pc = self._reset_vector_pc()
        self._registers = [0] * 16
        return ""

    def _reset_vector_pc(self) -> int:
        """PC on reset (SLAU367P §4.3, §1.2): fetched from the reset vector at
        0xFFFE/0xFFFF (little-endian word). Defaults to 0x4000 — FRAM code
        start (SLASE54D memory map) — when the vector has not been written.
        """
        lo = self._memory.get(0xFFFE)
        hi = self._memory.get(0xFFFF)
        if lo is None and hi is None:
            return 0x4000
        return ((hi or 0) << 8) | (lo or 0)

    def _cpu_halt(self, cmd: ScpiCommand) -> str:
        self._halted = True
        self._running = False
        return ""

    def _cpu_run(self, cmd: ScpiCommand) -> str:
        self._running = True
        self._halted = False
        return ""

    def _cpu_state(self, cmd: ScpiCommand) -> str:
        if self._halted:
            return "HALTED"
        if self._running:
            return "RUNNING"
        return "STOPPED"

    def _cpu_pc(self, cmd: ScpiCommand) -> str:
        """Program counter (SLAU367P §4.3.1): 20-bit, bit 0 always 0 (word-aligned)."""
        if cmd.is_query:
            return f"0x{self._pc:04X}"
        if cmd.params:
            v = int(cmd.params[0], 0)
            if not 0 <= v <= 0xFFFFF:
                raise ScpiError(-222, "PC out of range (0-0xFFFFF)")
            if v & 1:
                raise ScpiError(-222, "PC must be word-aligned (bit 0 is always 0)")
            self._pc = v
        return ""

    def _cpu_reg(self, cmd: ScpiCommand) -> str:
        """R0-R15 (SLAU367P §4.3): CPUX registers are 20-bit, masked accordingly."""
        if not cmd.params:
            raise ScpiError(-109, "Missing register number")
        reg = int(cmd.params[0])
        if not 0 <= reg <= 15:
            raise ScpiError(-222, "Register number out of range (0-15)")
        if cmd.is_query or len(cmd.params) < 2:
            return f"0x{self._registers[reg]:04X}"
        self._registers[reg] = int(cmd.params[1], 0) & 0xFFFFF
        return ""

    def _cpu_speed(self, cmd: ScpiCommand) -> str:
        if cmd.is_query:
            return f"{self._dco_actual():.0f}"
        if cmd.params:
            self.clock.dco_frequency = float(cmd.params[0])
        return ""

    def _cpu_vcc(self, cmd: ScpiCommand) -> str:
        if cmd.is_query:
            return f"{self.clock.vcc:.3f}"
        if cmd.params:
            v = float(cmd.params[0])
            if not 1.8 <= v <= 3.6:
                raise ScpiError(-222, "VCC out of range (1.8-3.6V)")
            self.clock.vcc = v
        return ""

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Clock handlers
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _clk_mclk_src(self, cmd: ScpiCommand) -> str:
        """MCLK source (SLAU367P §3.3.2 CSCTL2.SELM): DCO/LFXT/HFXT/VLO/MODCLK/LFMODCLK."""
        if cmd.is_query:
            return self.clock.mclk_source
        if cmd.params:
            v = cmd.params[0].upper()
            if v not in VALID_MCLK_SMCLK_SOURCES:
                raise ScpiError(-224, f"Illegal clock source: {v}")
            self.clock.mclk_source = v
        return ""

    def _clk_mclk_div(self, cmd: ScpiCommand) -> str:
        """MCLK divider (SLAU367P §3.3.3 CSCTL3.DIVM): /1-/32, powers of two only."""
        if cmd.is_query:
            return str(self.clock.mclk_div)
        if cmd.params:
            v = int(cmd.params[0])
            if v not in VALID_CLOCK_DIVIDERS:
                raise ScpiError(-222, f"Illegal divider: {v}")
            self.clock.mclk_div = v
        return ""

    def _clk_smclk_src(self, cmd: ScpiCommand) -> str:
        """SMCLK source (SLAU367P §3.3.2 CSCTL2.SELS): same mux as MCLK."""
        if cmd.is_query:
            return self.clock.smclk_source
        if cmd.params:
            v = cmd.params[0].upper()
            if v not in VALID_MCLK_SMCLK_SOURCES:
                raise ScpiError(-224, f"Illegal clock source: {v}")
            self.clock.smclk_source = v
        return ""

    def _clk_smclk_div(self, cmd: ScpiCommand) -> str:
        """SMCLK divider (SLAU367P §3.3.3 CSCTL3.DIVS): /1-/32, powers of two only."""
        if cmd.is_query:
            return str(self.clock.smclk_div)
        if cmd.params:
            v = int(cmd.params[0])
            if v not in VALID_CLOCK_DIVIDERS:
                raise ScpiError(-222, f"Illegal divider: {v}")
            self.clock.smclk_div = v
        return ""

    def _clk_aclk_src(self, cmd: ScpiCommand) -> str:
        """ACLK source (SLAU367P §3.3.2 CSCTL2.SELA): LFXT/VLO/LFMODCLK only."""
        if cmd.is_query:
            return self.clock.aclk_source
        if cmd.params:
            v = cmd.params[0].upper()
            if v not in VALID_ACLK_SOURCES:
                raise ScpiError(-224, f"Illegal clock source: {v}")
            self.clock.aclk_source = v
        return ""

    def _clk_aclk_div(self, cmd: ScpiCommand) -> str:
        """ACLK divider (SLAU367P §3.3.3 CSCTL3.DIVA): /1-/32, powers of two only."""
        if cmd.is_query:
            return str(self.clock.aclk_div)
        if cmd.params:
            v = int(cmd.params[0])
            if v not in VALID_CLOCK_DIVIDERS:
                raise ScpiError(-222, f"Illegal divider: {v}")
            self.clock.aclk_div = v
        return ""

    def _clk_dco_freq(self, cmd: ScpiCommand) -> str:
        if cmd.is_query:
            return f"{self._dco_actual():.0f}"
        if cmd.params:
            self.clock.dco_frequency = float(cmd.params[0])
        return ""

    def _dco_actual(self) -> float:
        """Effective DCO frequency: nominal setting × fault-profile drift."""
        return self.clock.dco_frequency * self.faults.dco_factor()

    def _clock_source_frequency(self, source: str) -> float:
        """Effective frequency (Hz) of one clock-system source, pre-divider.

        SLAU367P §3.2: DCO is the drift-affected trimmed oscillator
        (``_dco_actual()``); LFXT/HFXT read the crystal fields on
        ``ClockState``; VLO and MODCLK are fixed-frequency internal
        oscillators with no configurable register; LFMODCLK is MODCLK/128.
        """
        if source == "DCO":
            return self._dco_actual()
        if source == "LFXT":
            return self.clock.lfxt_frequency
        if source == "HFXT":
            return self.clock.hfxt_frequency
        if source == "VLO":
            return VLO_FREQUENCY_HZ
        if source == "MODCLK":
            return MODCLK_FREQUENCY_HZ
        if source == "LFMODCLK":
            return LFMODCLK_FREQUENCY_HZ
        raise ScpiError(-221, f"No simulated frequency for clock source {source}")

    def _clk_mclk_freq(self, cmd: ScpiCommand) -> str:
        freq = self._clock_source_frequency(self.clock.mclk_source) / self.clock.mclk_div
        return f"{freq:.0f}"

    def _clk_smclk_freq(self, cmd: ScpiCommand) -> str:
        freq = self._clock_source_frequency(self.clock.smclk_source) / self.clock.smclk_div
        return f"{freq:.0f}"

    def _clk_aclk_freq(self, cmd: ScpiCommand) -> str:
        freq = self._clock_source_frequency(self.clock.aclk_source) / self.clock.aclk_div
        return f"{freq:.0f}"

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Power management
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _pm_mode(self, cmd: ScpiCommand) -> str:
        """Power mode (SLAU367P §1.4, §2.2.4): AM, LPM0-4, and LPMx.5 (LPM3.5, LPM4.5)."""
        VALID = {"AM", "LPM0", "LPM1", "LPM2", "LPM3", "LPM4", "LPM3.5", "LPM4.5"}
        if cmd.is_query:
            return self.pm.mode
        if cmd.params:
            v = cmd.params[0].upper()
            if v not in VALID:
                raise ScpiError(-224, f"Illegal power mode: {v}")
            self.pm.mode = v
        return ""

    def _pm_wakeup(self, cmd: ScpiCommand) -> str:
        if cmd.is_query:
            return self.pm.wakeup_source
        if cmd.params:
            self.pm.wakeup_source = cmd.params[0].upper()
            self.pm.mode = "AM"
        return ""

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Memory access
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _mem_read(self, cmd: ScpiCommand) -> str:
        if not cmd.params:
            raise ScpiError(-109, "Missing address parameter")
        addr = int(cmd.params[0], 0)
        n = int(cmd.params[1]) if len(cmd.params) > 1 else 1
        result = []
        for i in range(n):
            result.append(f"0x{self._memory.get(addr + i, 0):02X}")
        return ",".join(result)

    def _mem_write(self, cmd: ScpiCommand) -> str:
        if len(cmd.params) < 2:
            raise ScpiError(-109, "Missing parameters: address, value")
        addr = int(cmd.params[0], 0)
        value = int(cmd.params[1], 0)
        self._memory[addr] = value & 0xFF
        return ""

    def _mem_fill(self, cmd: ScpiCommand) -> str:
        if len(cmd.params) < 3:
            raise ScpiError(-109, "Missing parameters: address, count, value")
        addr = int(cmd.params[0], 0)
        count = int(cmd.params[1])
        value = int(cmd.params[2], 0) & 0xFF
        for i in range(count):
            self._memory[addr + i] = value
        return ""

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # WDT (Watchdog Timer)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _wdt_state(self, cmd: ScpiCommand) -> str:
        if cmd.is_query:
            return "RUNNING"
        return ""

    def _wdt_password(self, cmd: ScpiCommand) -> str:
        return ""

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Fault/drift profiles (tolerances from SLASE54D; see msp430_faults)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _fault_profile(self, cmd: ScpiCommand, attr: str) -> str:
        """Get/set one peripheral's fault profile (NOMINAL or CORNER)."""
        if cmd.is_query:
            return getattr(self.faults, attr)
        if cmd.params:
            v = cmd.params[0].upper()
            if v not in PROFILES:
                raise ScpiError(-224, f"Illegal fault profile: {v}")
            setattr(self.faults, attr, v)
        return ""

    def _fault_profile_all(self, cmd: ScpiCommand) -> str:
        """Get/set every peripheral's fault profile at once."""
        if cmd.is_query:
            profiles = {self.faults.adc_profile, self.faults.clock_profile,
                        self.faults.timer_profile}
            return profiles.pop() if len(profiles) == 1 else "MIXED"
        if cmd.params:
            v = cmd.params[0].upper()
            if v not in PROFILES:
                raise ScpiError(-224, f"Illegal fault profile: {v}")
            self.faults.adc_profile = v
            self.faults.clock_profile = v
            self.faults.timer_profile = v
        return ""

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Interrupt system
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _int_enable(self, cmd: ScpiCommand) -> str:
        return ""

    def _int_disable(self, cmd: ScpiCommand) -> str:
        return ""

    def _int_vector(self, cmd: ScpiCommand) -> str:
        if cmd.is_query:
            return "0xFFFF"
        return ""

    def _int_flag(self, cmd: ScpiCommand) -> str:
        if cmd.is_query:
            return "0"
        return ""

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Reset
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _do_reset(self) -> None:
        self.ports = {i: GPIOPort() for i in range(1, self.NUM_PORTS + 1)}
        self.adc = {i: ADCChannel() for i in range(self.NUM_ADC_CH)}
        self.timer_a = {i: TimerState() for i in range(self.NUM_TIMER_A)}
        self.timer_b = {i: TimerState() for i in range(self.NUM_TIMER_B)}
        self.uart = {i: UARTState() for i in range(self.NUM_UART)}
        self.spi = {i: SPIState() for i in range(self.NUM_SPI)}
        self.i2c = {i: I2CState() for i in range(self.NUM_I2C)}
        self.clock = ClockState()
        self.pm = PMState()
        self.faults.reset_profiles()
        self.faults.resample()  # part-to-part signs re-sampled per *RST, not per read
        self._veref_v = 1.2
        self._memory = {}
        self._running = False
        self._halted = False
        self._pc = self._reset_vector_pc()
        self._registers = [0] * 16
        self._setup_handlers()

"""Base class for all simulated SCPI instruments."""

from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Dict, Callable, Optional, List
from silmulator.scpi.parser import ScpiParser, ScpiCommand
import logging

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class ScpiError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, code: int, msg: str):
        self.code = code
        self.msg = msg
        super().__init__(f"SCPI Error {code}: {msg}")


ERROR_MSGS = {
    -100: "Command error",
    -101: "Invalid character",
    -102: "Syntax error",
    -103: "Invalid separator",
    -104: "Data type error",
    -108: "Parameter not allowed",
    -109: "Missing parameter",
    -113: "Undefined header",
    -120: "Numeric data error",
    -121: "Invalid character in number",
    -123: "Exponent too large",
    -124: "Too many digits",
    -128: "Numeric data not allowed",
    -131: "Invalid suffix",
    -138: "Suffix not allowed",
    -148: "Character data not allowed",
    -150: "String data error",
    -151: "Invalid string data",
    -158: "String data not allowed",
    -160: "Block data error",
    -168: "Block data not allowed",
    -170: "Expression error",
    -178: "Expression data not allowed",
    -200: "Execution error",
    -220: "Parameter error",
    -221: "Settings conflict",
    -222: "Data out of range",
    -223: "Too much data",
    -224: "Illegal parameter value",
    -241: "Hardware missing",
    -310: "System error",
    -350: "Queue overflow",
    -410: "Query interrupted",
    -420: "Query unterminated",
    -430: "Query deadlocked",
    -440: "Query UNTERMINATED after indefinite response",
}


class BaseDevice:
    """Abstract base for all simulated SCPI instruments.

    Subclasses register handlers via `_register(path, fn)`.
    `process(cmd_string)` dispatches to the right handler.
    """

    MANUFACTURER = "Silmulator"
    MODEL = "BASE"
    SERIAL = "SIM000001"
    FIRMWARE = "1.0.0"

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._parser = ScpiParser()
        self._handlers: Dict[str, Callable[[ScpiCommand], str]] = {}
        self._error_queue: List[tuple[int, str]] = []
        self._event_status_register: int = 0
        self._event_status_enable: int = 0
        self._service_request_enable: int = 0
        self._operation_complete: bool = False
        self._output_queue: List[str] = []
        self._setup_common_handlers()
        self._setup_handlers()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Public interface
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def process(self, raw: str) -> str:
        """Process one or more SCPI commands and return response string."""
        responses: List[str] = []
        try:
            commands = self._parser.parse(raw.strip())
        except Exception as e:
            self._push_error(-100, str(e))
            return ""

        for cmd in commands:
            try:
                resp = self._dispatch(cmd)
                if resp is not None and resp != "":
                    responses.append(resp)
            except ScpiError as e:
                self._push_error(e.code, e.msg)
            except Exception as e:
                logger.exception("Unhandled error processing %s", cmd)
                self._push_error(-200, str(e))

        return "\n".join(responses)

    def reset(self) -> None:
        """Reset device to factory defaults."""
        self._error_queue.clear()
        self._event_status_register = 0
        self._event_status_enable = 0
        self._service_request_enable = 0
        self._operation_complete = False
        self._do_reset()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Registration helpers
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _register(self, path: str, fn: Callable[[ScpiCommand], str]) -> None:
        self._handlers[path.upper()] = fn

    def _register_alias(self, alias: str, target: str) -> None:
        target_upper = target.upper()
        def handler(cmd: ScpiCommand) -> str:
            return self._handlers[target_upper](cmd)
        self._handlers[alias.upper()] = handler

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Common IEEE 488.2 handlers
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _setup_common_handlers(self) -> None:
        self._register("*IDN", self._idn)
        self._register("*RST", self._rst)
        self._register("*CLS", self._cls)
        self._register("*ESE", self._ese)
        self._register("*ESR", self._esr)
        self._register("*OPC", self._opc)
        self._register("*SRE", self._sre)
        self._register("*STB", self._stb)
        self._register("*TST", self._tst)
        self._register("*WAI", self._wai)
        self._register("SYSTEM:ERROR", self._sys_error)
        self._register("SYSTEM:ERROR:NEXT", self._sys_error)
        self._register("SYSTEM:ERROR:COUNT", self._sys_error_count)
        self._register("SYSTEM:VERSION", self._sys_version)

    def _idn(self, cmd: ScpiCommand) -> str:
        return f"{self.MANUFACTURER},{self.MODEL},{self.SERIAL},{self.FIRMWARE}"

    def _rst(self, cmd: ScpiCommand) -> str:
        self.reset()
        return ""

    def _cls(self, cmd: ScpiCommand) -> str:
        self._error_queue.clear()
        self._event_status_register = 0
        return ""

    def _ese(self, cmd: ScpiCommand) -> str:
        if cmd.is_query:
            return str(self._event_status_enable)
        if cmd.params:
            self._event_status_enable = int(float(cmd.params[0]))
        return ""

    def _esr(self, cmd: ScpiCommand) -> str:
        val = self._event_status_register
        self._event_status_register = 0
        return str(val)

    def _opc(self, cmd: ScpiCommand) -> str:
        if cmd.is_query:
            return "1"
        self._operation_complete = True
        self._event_status_register |= 1
        return ""

    def _sre(self, cmd: ScpiCommand) -> str:
        if cmd.is_query:
            return str(self._service_request_enable)
        if cmd.params:
            self._service_request_enable = int(float(cmd.params[0]))
        return ""

    def _stb(self, cmd: ScpiCommand) -> str:
        stb = 0
        if self._error_queue:
            stb |= 4
        if self._event_status_register & self._event_status_enable:
            stb |= 32
        if stb & self._service_request_enable:
            stb |= 64
        return str(stb)

    def _tst(self, cmd: ScpiCommand) -> str:
        return "0"  # Self-test passed

    def _wai(self, cmd: ScpiCommand) -> str:
        return ""

    def _sys_error(self, cmd: ScpiCommand) -> str:
        if self._error_queue:
            code, msg = self._error_queue.pop(0)
            return f'{code},"{msg}"'
        return '0,"No error"'

    def _sys_error_count(self, cmd: ScpiCommand) -> str:
        return str(len(self._error_queue))

    def _sys_version(self, cmd: ScpiCommand) -> str:
        return "1999.0"

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Dispatch
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _dispatch(self, cmd: ScpiCommand) -> str:
        path = cmd.path.upper()
        handler = self._handlers.get(path)
        if handler is None:
            # Try partial match for compound paths
            raise ScpiError(-113, f"Undefined header: {path}")
        return handler(cmd)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Error management
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _push_error(self, code: int, msg: Optional[str] = None) -> None:
        if msg is None:
            msg = ERROR_MSGS.get(code, "Unknown error")
        if len(self._error_queue) < 20:
            self._error_queue.append((code, msg))
        else:
            self._error_queue[-1] = (-350, "Queue overflow")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Subclass hooks
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _setup_handlers(self) -> None:
        """Subclasses override to register device-specific handlers."""

    def _do_reset(self) -> None:
        """Subclasses override to reset device-specific state."""

"""Spec-driven edge-case tests for the MSP430 simulator.

Each test cites the TI document section it verifies (SLAU367P User's Guide /
SLASE54D datasheet — the copies in ``hardware_docs/ti/MSP430FR5994/``).

Behaviors the current model gets wrong are marked ``xfail(strict=True)`` with
the matching finding from ``docs/audits/msp430-compliance-report.md``. That is
the plan's "captured failure list": fixing ``msp430.py`` makes the marker fail
loudly (XPASS) so it gets removed deliberately, never silently.
"""
import pytest

from silmulator.devices.msp430 import MSP430


@pytest.fixture
def mcu():
    return MSP430()


def errors(mcu) -> int:
    """Depth of the device SCPI error queue."""
    return len(mcu._error_queue)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# GPIO — SLAU367P §12 (Digital I/O)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class TestGPIOEdgeCases:
    def test_direction_mask_boundaries(self, mcu):
        # SLAU367P §12.2.3: PxDIR is an 8-bit register; 0x00 and 0xFF are the extremes.
        mcu.process("GPIO:PORT1:DIRECTION 0x00")
        assert mcu.process("GPIO:PORT1:DIRECTION?") == "0x00"
        mcu.process("GPIO:PORT1:DIRECTION 0xFF")
        assert mcu.process("GPIO:PORT1:DIRECTION?") == "0xFF"
        assert errors(mcu) == 0

    def test_direction_write_masks_to_8_bits(self, mcu):
        # SLAU367P §12.2.3: ports are 8 bits wide; excess bits cannot be stored.
        mcu.process("GPIO:PORT1:DIRECTION 0x1FF")
        assert mcu.process("GPIO:PORT1:DIRECTION?") == "0xFF"

    def test_pin_direction_valid_boundary_pins(self, mcu):
        # SLAU367P §12.2.3: pins 0 and 7 are the valid extremes of an 8-bit port.
        mcu.process("GPIO:PORT1:PIN:DIRECTION 0,OUTPUT")
        mcu.process("GPIO:PORT1:PIN:DIRECTION 7,OUTPUT")
        assert int(mcu.process("GPIO:PORT1:DIRECTION?"), 16) == 0x81
        assert errors(mcu) == 0

    def test_pin_index_beyond_port_width_rejected(self, mcu):
        # SLAU367P §12.2: each port has exactly 8 I/O lines; pin 12 does not exist.
        mcu.process("GPIO:PORT1:PIN:VALUE 12,1")
        assert errors(mcu) == 1
        assert mcu.ports[1].output <= 0xFF

    def test_invalid_pin_mode_rejected(self, mcu):
        # SLAU367P §12.2.3: a pin is input (0) or output (1); no other mode exists.
        mcu.process("GPIO:PORT1:PIN:DIRECTION 0,BANANA")
        assert errors(mcu) == 1

    def test_pullup_pulldown_mutually_exclusive(self, mcu):
        # SLAU367P §12.2.4, Table 12-1: PxREN enables one resistor whose direction
        # is PxOUT's bit — pull-up and pull-down cannot both be active.
        mcu.process("GPIO:PORT1:PULLUP 0x01")
        mcu.process("GPIO:PORT1:PULLDOWN 0x01")
        assert not (mcu.ports[1].pullup & mcu.ports[1].pulldown)

    def test_input_reflects_enabled_pullup(self, mcu):
        # SLAU367P §12.2.4: with the pin as input and the pull-up enabled, an
        # undriven pin reads high.
        mcu.process("GPIO:PORT1:DIRECTION 0x00")
        mcu.process("GPIO:PORT1:PULLUP 0x01")
        assert int(mcu.process("GPIO:PORT1:INPUT?"), 16) & 0x01 == 0x01


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ADC — SLAU367P §34 (ADC12_B), §33 (REF_A); SLASE54D §8.12.9
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class TestADCEdgeCases:
    def test_resolution_valid_values(self, mcu):
        # SLAU367P §34.3 (ADC12CTL2.ADC12RES): 8-, 10-, and 12-bit modes exist.
        for res in (8, 10, 12):
            mcu.process(f"ADC:RESOLUTION {res}")
            assert mcu.process("ADC:RESOLUTION?") == str(res)
        assert errors(mcu) == 0

    def test_resolution_invalid_rejected(self, mcu):
        # SLAU367P §34.3: ADC12RES has no 14-bit encoding.
        mcu.process("ADC:RESOLUTION 14")
        assert errors(mcu) == 1

    def test_raw_full_scale_at_reference_voltage(self, mcu):
        # SLAU367P §34.2.1 Eq. 13: NADC is full scale (0FFFh) when Vin >= VR+.
        mcu.inject_adc(0, 3.3)
        assert int(mcu.process("ADC:CHANNEL0:RAW?")) == 4095

    def test_raw_saturates_above_reference(self, mcu):
        # SLAU367P §34.2.1 Eq. 15: output saturates at full scale above VR+.
        mcu.inject_adc(0, 5.0)
        assert int(mcu.process("ADC:CHANNEL0:RAW?")) == 4095

    def test_raw_clamps_to_zero_below_vr_minus(self, mcu):
        # SLAU367P §34.2.1: NADC is zero when the input is at or below VR-.
        mcu.inject_adc(0, -1.0)
        assert int(mcu.process("ADC:CHANNEL0:RAW?")) == 0

    def test_resolution_scales_full_range(self, mcu):
        # SLAU367P §34.3 (ADC12RES): 8-bit mode has a 255-count full scale.
        mcu.process("ADC:RESOLUTION 8")
        mcu.inject_adc(0, 3.3)
        assert int(mcu.process("ADC:CHANNEL0:RAW?")) == 255

    def test_reference_out_of_range_rejected(self, mcu):
        # SLAU367P §34.2.4 (ADC12VRSEL), §33 (REF_A): the reference is selected
        # from a fixed set (AVCC, 1.2/2.0/2.5-V REF, external) — not free-form.
        mcu.process("ADC:REFERENCE BANANA")
        assert errors(mcu) == 1

    def test_raw_respects_selected_reference(self, mcu):
        # SLAU367P §34.2.1 Eq. 13: with VR+ = 1.2-V VREF, a 1.2-V input is full scale.
        mcu.process("ADC:REFERENCE VREF")
        mcu.inject_adc(0, 1.2)
        assert int(mcu.process("ADC:CHANNEL0:RAW?")) == 4095

    def test_veref_voltage_param_must_be_numeric(self, mcu):
        # A malformed VeREF+ voltage must queue a SCPI error, not crash the
        # handler (ADC:REFERENCE VEREF,<v> takes a board-supplied voltage).
        mcu.process("ADC:REFERENCE VEREF,notanumber")
        assert errors(mcu) == 1

    @pytest.mark.xfail(
        strict=True,
        reason="audit ADC:CONVERT (NON_COMPLIANT): conversions run without the "
               "ADC12ENC enable gate",
    )
    def test_conversion_requires_enable(self, mcu):
        # SLAU367P §34.2 (ADC12ENC): 'ADC12ENC must be set to 1 before any
        # conversion can take place.'
        mcu.inject_adc(0, 1.0)
        mcu.process("ADC:CONVERT 0")
        assert errors(mcu) == 1  # channel/module was never enabled

    @pytest.mark.xfail(
        strict=True,
        reason="audit ADC:CONVERT: nonexistent channel returns '0' with no error",
    )
    def test_convert_invalid_channel_rejected(self, mcu):
        # SLASE54D Table 6-1: the FR5994 exposes a bounded ADC channel set; a
        # conversion on a channel that does not exist is an error, not a zero.
        mcu.process("ADC:CONVERT 99")
        assert errors(mcu) == 1


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Timer_A — SLAU367P §25; SLASE54D Table 6-1
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class TestTimerAEdgeCases:
    def test_mode_valid_set(self, mcu):
        # SLAU367P §25.2.3 (MC bits): stop, up, continuous, up/down.
        for mode in ("STOP", "UP", "CONTINUOUS", "UPDOWN"):
            mcu.process(f"TIMERA0:MODE {mode}")
            assert mcu.process("TIMERA0:MODE?") == mode
        assert errors(mcu) == 0

    def test_mode_invalid_rejected(self, mcu):
        # SLAU367P §25.2.3: MC has exactly four encodings.
        mcu.process("TIMERA0:MODE BANANA")
        assert errors(mcu) == 1

    def test_clock_source_valid_set(self, mcu):
        # SLAU367P §25.3.1 (TASSEL): TACLK, ACLK, SMCLK, INCLK.
        for src in ("TACLK", "ACLK", "SMCLK", "INCLK"):
            mcu.process(f"TIMERA0:CLOCK:SOURCE {src}")
            assert mcu.process("TIMERA0:CLOCK:SOURCE?") == src
        assert errors(mcu) == 0

    def test_clock_source_invalid_rejected(self, mcu):
        # SLAU367P §25.3.1: TASSEL has four encodings.
        mcu.process("TIMERA0:CLOCK:SOURCE BANANA")
        assert errors(mcu) == 1

    def test_divider_valid_boundaries(self, mcu):
        # SLAU367P §25.2.1.1: ID (/1../8) x TAIDEX (/1../8) reaches /1 and /64.
        mcu.process("TIMERA0:CLOCK:DIVIDER 1")
        assert mcu.process("TIMERA0:CLOCK:DIVIDER?") == "1"
        mcu.process("TIMERA0:CLOCK:DIVIDER 64")
        assert mcu.process("TIMERA0:CLOCK:DIVIDER?") == "64"
        assert errors(mcu) == 0

    def test_divider_128_rejected(self, mcu):
        # SLAU367P §25.2.1.1: no ID x TAIDEX combination produces /128.
        mcu.process("TIMERA0:CLOCK:DIVIDER 128")
        assert errors(mcu) == 1

    def test_count_16bit_maximum(self, mcu):
        # SLAU367P §25.2.1: TAxR is 16 bits; 0xFFFF is the last valid count.
        mcu.process("TIMERA0:COUNT 0xFFFF")
        assert int(mcu.process("TIMERA0:COUNT?")) == 0xFFFF

    def test_count_over_16bit_rejected_or_masked(self, mcu):
        # SLAU367P §25.2.1: a 16-bit counter cannot hold 0x10000.
        mcu.process("TIMERA0:COUNT 0x10000")
        assert errors(mcu) == 1 or mcu.timer_a[0].count <= 0xFFFF

    def test_capture_compare_boundary_value(self, mcu):
        # SLAU367P §25.2.4: TAxCCRn is a 16-bit compare register.
        mcu.process("TIMERA0:CC0:VALUE 0xFFFF")
        assert int(mcu.process("TIMERA0:CC0:VALUE?")) == 0xFFFF

    def test_capture_mode_settable(self, mcu):
        # SLAU367P §25.2.4 (CAP bit): each CC unit supports capture mode.
        mcu.process("TIMERA0:CC1:MODE CAPTURE")
        assert mcu.process("TIMERA0:CC1:MODE?") == "CAPTURE"

    @pytest.mark.xfail(
        strict=True,
        reason="audit TIMERAn:CCn:VALUE (PARTIAL): model exposes CCR0-3 on every "
               "instance; FR5994 Timer_A instances have 3,3,2,2,2 CC registers",
    )
    def test_ta0_ccr3_does_not_exist(self, mcu):
        # SLASE54D Table 6-1: TA0 has three CC registers (CCR0-CCR2).
        mcu.process("TIMERA0:CC3:VALUE 100")
        assert errors(mcu) == 1  # undefined header on real hardware

    def test_period_is_ccr0_in_up_mode(self, mcu):
        # SLAU367P §25.2.3.1: in up mode the period register IS TAxCCR0.
        mcu.process("TIMERA0:MODE UP")
        mcu.process("TIMERA0:PERIOD 1000")
        assert int(mcu.process("TIMERA0:CC0:VALUE?")) == 1000


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Clock system and PMM boundaries — SLAU367P §3, §2; SLASE54D §8.3
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class TestClockAndPowerEdgeCases:
    def test_mclk_divider_32_boundary(self, mcu):
        # SLAU367P §3.3.3 (CSCTL3.DIVM): /32 is the maximum divider.
        mcu.process("CLOCK:MCLK:DIVIDER 32")
        assert mcu.process("CLOCK:MCLK:DIVIDER?") == "32"
        assert errors(mcu) == 0

    def test_mclk_divider_64_rejected(self, mcu):
        # SLAU367P §3.3.3: DIVM encodings stop at /32.
        mcu.process("CLOCK:MCLK:DIVIDER 64")
        assert errors(mcu) == 1

    def test_mclk_source_modclk_accepted(self, mcu):
        # SLAU367P §3.3.2 (CSCTL2.SELM): MODCLK is encoding 4.
        mcu.process("CLOCK:MCLK:SOURCE MODCLK")
        assert errors(mcu) == 0
        assert mcu.process("CLOCK:MCLK:SOURCE?") == "MODCLK"

    def test_lpm35_accepted(self, mcu):
        # SLAU367P §2.2.4: 'LPM3.5 and LPM4.5 are additional low-power modes'.
        mcu.process("POWER:MODE LPM3.5")
        assert errors(mcu) == 0
        assert mcu.process("POWER:MODE?") == "LPM3.5"

    def test_vcc_boundaries(self, mcu):
        # SLASE54D §8.3: supply range is 1.8 V to 3.6 V inclusive.
        mcu.process("CPU:VCC 1.8")
        mcu.process("CPU:VCC 3.6")
        assert errors(mcu) == 0
        mcu.process("CPU:VCC 1.7")
        assert errors(mcu) == 1
        mcu.process("CPU:VCC 3.7")
        assert errors(mcu) == 2

1	"""Pure-Python SCPI command parser. Used as fallback when C++ core is unavailable."""
2	
3	from __future__ import annotations
4	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
5	from typing import List, Optional
6	import re
7	
8	
9	@dataclass
10	class ScpiCommand:
11	    path: str = ""
12	    is_query: bool = False
13	    params: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
14	
15	    def __repr__(self) -> str:
16	        return f"<ScpiCommand path={self.path!r} query={self.is_query}>"
17	
18	
19	class ScpiParser:
20	    """Parse SCPI command strings into ScpiCommand objects.
21	
22	    Supports:
23	    - Compound commands separated by ';'
24	    - Query suffix '?'
25	    - Relative and absolute path notation
26	    - Common data types (NR1, NR2, NR3, strings, boolean mnemonics)
27	    """
28	
29	    BOOLEAN_TRUE = {"ON", "1", "TRUE", "YES"}
30	    BOOLEAN_FALSE = {"OFF", "0", "FALSE", "NO"}
31	
32	    def __init__(self) -> None:
33	        self._current_root: str = ""
34	
35	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
36	    # Public API
37	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
38	
39	    def parse(self, raw: str) -> List[ScpiCommand]:
40	        cmds = []
41	        parts = self.split_compound(raw)
42	        first = True
43	        for part in parts:
44	            part = part.strip()
45	            if part:
46	                cmds.append(self._parse_single(part, reset_root=first))
47	                first = False
48	        return cmds
49	
50	    @staticmethod
51	    def split_compound(raw: str) -> List[str]:
52	        parts: List[str] = []
53	        current = ""
54	        in_quote = False
55	        quote_char = ""
56	        for ch in raw:
57	            if not in_quote and ch in ("'", '"'):
58	                in_quote = True
59	                quote_char = ch
60	                current += ch
61	            elif in_quote and ch == quote_char:
62	                in_quote = False
63	                current += ch
64	            elif not in_quote and ch == ";":
65	                parts.append(current.strip())
66	                current = ""
67	            else:
68	                current += ch
69	        if current.strip():
70	            parts.append(current.strip())
71	        return parts
72	
73	    @staticmethod
74	    def normalize_header(hdr: str) -> str:
75	        parts = [p.upper() for p in hdr.split(":") if p]
76	        return ":".join(parts)
77	
78	    @staticmethod
79	    def coerce_number(s: str) -> Optional[float]:
80	        try:
81	            return float(s)
82	        except (ValueError, TypeError):
83	            return None
84	
85	    @staticmethod
86	    def coerce_bool(s: str) -> Optional[bool]:
87	        upper = s.upper()
88	        if upper in ScpiParser.BOOLEAN_TRUE:
89	            return True
90	        if upper in ScpiParser.BOOLEAN_FALSE:
91	            return False
92	        return None
93	
94	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
95	    # Private helpers
96	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
97	
98	    def _parse_single(self, cmd: str, reset_root: bool) -> ScpiCommand:
99	        sc = ScpiCommand()
100	        cmd = cmd.strip()
101	        if not cmd:
102	            return sc
103	
104	        # Split header from params on first whitespace
105	        m = re.match(r'^(\S+)([\s,](.*))?$', cmd, re.DOTALL)
106	        if not m:
107	            sc.path = self.normalize_header(cmd)
108	            return sc
109	
110	        header_raw = m.group(1)
111	        rest = (m.group(3) or "").strip()
112	
113	        # Detect query
114	        if header_raw.endswith("?"):
115	            sc.is_query = True
116	            header_raw = header_raw[:-1]
117	
118	        # Parse params
119	        if rest:
120	            sc.params = self._split_params(rest)
121	
122	        # Handle path hierarchy
123	        absolute = header_raw.startswith("*")
124	        rooted = header_raw.startswith(":")
125	        if rooted:
126	            header_raw = header_raw[1:]
127	
128	        if absolute or rooted or reset_root:
129	            self._current_root = ""
130	
131	        if self._current_root and not absolute and not rooted:
132	            # Relative: prepend parent of current root
133	            parent = self._current_root.rsplit(":", 1)[0] if ":" in self._current_root else ""
134	            prefix = parent + ":" if parent else ""
135	            sc.path = self.normalize_header(prefix + header_raw)
136	        else:
137	            sc.path = self.normalize_header(header_raw)
138	
139	        self._current_root = sc.path
140	        return sc
141	
142	    @staticmethod
143	    def _split_params(rest: str) -> List[str]:
144	        params: List[str] = []
145	        current = ""
146	        in_quote = False
147	        quote_char = ""
148	        for ch in rest:
149	            if not in_quote and ch in ("'", '"'):
150	                in_quote = True
151	                quote_char = ch
152	                current += ch
153	            elif in_quote and ch == quote_char:
154	                in_quote = False
155	                current += ch
156	            elif not in_quote and ch == ",":
157	                params.append(current.strip())
158	                current = ""
159	            else:
160	                current += ch
161	        if current.strip():
162	            params.append(current.strip())
163	        return params

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""SCPI compliance audit for ``silmulator/devices/msp430.py``.
3	
4	Scores every SCPI command family the simulated MSP430 implements against the
5	TI MSP430FR5994 documentation shipped in ``hardware_docs/ti/MSP430FR5994/``:
6	
7	- SLAU367P  — MSP430FR58xx/59xx/6xx Family User's Guide
8	- SLASE54D  — MSP430FR599x datasheet
9	
10	The audit is a curated findings database plus live behavioral probes.
11	Probes re-execute the questionable behavior against a fresh ``MSP430()``
12	instance every run, so the report stays honest as the device model evolves:
13	
14	- a command added to msp430.py without an audit entry is reported UNSCORED;
15	- a finding whose probe no longer reproduces is reported STALE (the model
16	  changed; the audit entry needs review).
17	
18	Usage:
19	    python scripts/audit_msp430.py [--output docs/audits/msp430-compliance-report.md]
20	
21	Exit code is 0 when the audit itself ran cleanly (findings are data, not
22	failures); 1 when there are UNSCORED commands or STALE findings.
23	"""
24	
25	from __future__ import annotations
26	
27	import argparse

101	def family(path: str) -> str:
102	    """Collapse an indexed SCPI path into its command family."""
103	    out = path
104	    for rx, repl in _FAMILY_SUBS:
105	        out = rx.sub(repl, out)
106	    return out

114	def _errors(dev: MSP430) -> int:
115	    """Number of queued SCPI errors on the device."""
116	    return len(dev._error_queue)
117

119	def probe_timer_divider_128(dev: MSP430) -> bool:
120	    """/128 is rejected — no ID×TAIDEX combination produces it (§25.2.1.1)."""
121	    dev.process("TIMERA0:CLOCK:DIVIDER 128")
122	    return _errors(dev) == 1 and dev.timer_a[0].clock_divider == 1
123

125	def probe_adc_ignores_reference(dev: MSP430) -> bool:
126	    """Raw conversion scales by the selected reference (SLAU367P §34.2.1 Eq. 13)."""
127	    dev.process("ADC:REFERENCE VREF")
128	    dev.inject_adc(0, 1.2)
129	    raw = int(dev.process("ADC:CHANNEL0:RAW?"))
130	    return raw == 4095  # 1.2 V vs 1.2-V VREF (REFVSEL reset default) is full scale

133	def probe_adc_convert_invalid_channel(dev: MSP430) -> bool:
134	    """Conversion on a nonexistent channel returns '0' instead of an error."""
135	    resp = dev.process("ADC:CONVERT 99")
136	    return resp == "0" and _errors(dev) == 0

158	def probe_cpu_reg_20bit(dev: MSP430) -> bool:
159	    """CPUX registers are 20-bit; the model masks writes to 20 bits (0xFFFFF)."""
160	    dev.process("CPU:REGISTER 4,0x12345")
161	    return dev.process("CPU:REGISTER? 4") == "0x12345"

164	def probe_cpu_pc_validated(dev: MSP430) -> bool:
165	    """PC rejects odd and >20-bit values that cannot exist in hardware."""
166	    dev.process("CPU:PC 0x123457")
167	    odd_and_wide_rejected = _errors(dev) == 1 and dev._pc != 0x123457
168	    dev.process("CPU:PC 0x4000")
169	    even_in_range_accepted = _errors(dev) == 1 and dev._pc == 0x4000
170	    return odd_and_wide_rejected and even_in_range_accepted
171

173	def probe_cpu_reset_vector_pc(dev: MSP430) -> bool:
174	    """CPU:RESET fetches PC from the reset vector at 0xFFFE, defaulting to 0x4000."""
175	    dev.process("CPU:RESET")
176	    default_ok = dev._pc == 0x4000
177	    dev.process('MEMORY:WRITE 0xFFFE,0x00')
178	    dev.process('MEMORY:WRITE 0xFFFF,0xC0')
179	    dev.process("CPU:RESET")
180	    vector_ok = dev._pc == 0xC000
181	    return default_ok and vector_ok

184	def probe_dco_freq_continuous(dev: MSP430) -> bool:
185	    """DCO accepts arbitrary frequencies; hardware has discrete DCOFSEL steps."""
186	    dev.process("CLOCK:DCO:FREQUENCY 3141592")
187	    return _errors(dev) == 0 and dev.clock.dco_frequency == 3141592.0

190	def probe_lpm35_accepted(dev: MSP430) -> bool:
191	    """LPM3.5 and LPM4.5 both exist on FR5994 (SLAU367P §2.2.4) and are accepted."""
192	    dev.process("POWER:MODE LPM3.5")
193	    lpm35_ok = _errors(dev) == 0 and dev.pm.mode == "LPM3.5"
194	    dev.process("POWER:MODE LPM4.5")
195	    lpm45_ok = _errors(dev) == 0 and dev.pm.mode == "LPM4.5"
196	    return lpm35_ok and lpm45_ok

199	def probe_mclk_source_set(dev: MSP430) -> bool:
200	    """MCLK's source set matches CSCTL2.SELM: MODCLK accepted, REFO rejected."""
201	    dev.process("CLOCK:MCLK:SOURCE MODCLK")
202	    accepted_modclk = _errors(dev) == 0 and dev.clock.mclk_source == "MODCLK"
203	    dev.process("CLOCK:MCLK:SOURCE REFO")

229	def probe_mclk_freq_ignores_source(dev: MSP430) -> bool:
230	    """MCLK:FREQUENCY? follows the selected source: LFXT-sourced MCLK reads LFXT/div."""
231	    dev.process("CLOCK:MCLK:SOURCE LFXT")

242	def probe_i2c_transfer_ignores_address(dev: MSP430) -> bool:
243	    """I2C TRANSFER parses a target address, then never uses it."""
244	    r1 = dev.process('I2C0:TRANSFER 0x50,"AB"')
245	    dev.reset()

251	    """I2C WRITE returns ACK unconditionally; no NACK path exists."""
252	    return dev.process('I2C0:WRITE "DEADBEEF"') == "ACK"

255	def probe_wdt_stub(dev: MSP430) -> bool:
256	    """WDT state cannot change and a wrong password does not cause a PUC."""
257	    pc_before = dev._pc
258	    dev.process("WDT:PASSWORD 0x1234")  # wrong password: real part resets
259	    state = dev.process("WDT:STATE?")
260	    return state == "RUNNING" and _errors(dev) == 0 and dev._pc == pc_before
261

263	def probe_interrupt_stub(dev: MSP430) -> bool:
264	    """Interrupt system is a stub: vector is a constant, flags always 0."""
265	    return (
266	        dev.process("INTERRUPT:VECTOR?") == "0xFFFF"
267	        and dev.process("INTERRUPT:FLAG?") == "0"
268	    )

272	    """Reads of vacant/impossible addresses return 0x00 with no error."""

274	    return resp == "0x00" and _errors(dev) == 0

295	def probe_gpio_pull_both(dev: MSP430) -> bool:
296	    """Pull-up and pull-down are mutually exclusive on one pin (one PxREN bit)."""

302	def probe_gpio_input_ignores_pulls(dev: MSP430) -> bool:
303	    """Undriven input pins with REN enabled read PxOUT's pull level (§12.2.4)."""
304	    dev.process("GPIO:PORT1:DIRECTION 0x00")

306	    dev.process("GPIO:PORT1:OUTPUT 0xFF")
307	    return dev.process("GPIO:PORT1:INPUT?") == "0xFF"

731	    "Capacitive Touch I/O (SLAU367P §13)",
732	]
733	
734	
735	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
736	# Audit engine
737	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
738	
739	def run_audit() -> Tuple[Dict[str, List[str]], List[str], List[str]]:
740	    """Map handler paths to families; run probes.
741	
742	    Returns (family → concrete paths, unscored families, stale probe names).
743	    """
744	    dev = MSP430()
745	    fam_paths: Dict[str, List[str]] = {}
746	    for path in sorted(dev._handlers):
747	        fam_paths.setdefault(family(path), []).append(path)
748	
749	    unscored = sorted(f for f in fam_paths if f not in FINDINGS)
750	
751	    stale: List[str] = []
752	    for name, probe in PROBES.items():
753	        if not probe(MSP430()):
754	            stale.append(name)
755	    return fam_paths, unscored, stale
756	
757	
758	def render_report(fam_paths: Dict[str, List[str]], unscored: List[str],
759	                  stale: List[str]) -> str:
760	    """Render the Markdown compliance report."""
761	    scored = {f: v for f, v in FINDINGS.items() if v.score in SCORED and f in fam_paths}
762	    tally = {s: sum(1 for v in scored.values() if v.score == s) for s in SCORED}
763	    total_scored = sum(tally.values())
764	    pct = 100.0 * tally[COMPLIANT] / total_scored if total_scored else 0.0
765	
766	    by_subsystem: Dict[str, List[Tuple[str, Finding]]] = {}
767	    for fam, finding in FINDINGS.items():
768	        if fam in fam_paths:
769	            by_subsystem.setdefault(finding.subsystem, []).append((fam, finding))
770	
771	    lines: List[str] = []
772	    a = lines.append
773	    a("# MSP430 SCPI Compliance Report")
774	    a("")
775	    a("Audit of `silmulator/devices/msp430.py` against TI documentation.")
776	    a("")
777	    a("| Ground truth | Revision |")
778	    a("|---|---|")
779	    a("| MSP430FR58xx/59xx/6xx Family User's Guide | **SLAU367P** |")
780	    a("| MSP430FR599x datasheet | **SLASE54D** |")
781	    a("")
782	    a("Generated by `scripts/audit_msp430.py` — re-run it after changing "
783	      "`msp430.py`; probes verify each mechanical finding still reproduces.")
784	    a("")
785	    a("## Scope and method")
786	    a("")
787	    a("Every registered SCPI path is collapsed into a command family "
788	      f"({sum(len(p) for p in fam_paths.values())} paths → {len(fam_paths)} families) "
789	      "and each family is scored:")
790	    a("")
791	    a("- **COMPLIANT** — matches the doc for typical use and boundary values")
792	    a("- **PARTIAL** — right concept, misses documented edge cases or side effects")
793	    a("- **NON_COMPLIANT** — contradicts the doc for typical use")
794	    a("- **ACCEPTS_INVALID** — silently accepts states the doc says cannot exist "
795	      "(own category per the audit plan)")
796	    a("- **UNDOCUMENTED** — simulator convenience with no doc basis (outside the score)")
797	    a("- **FRAMEWORK** — IEEE-488.2/SCPI plumbing from `BaseDevice` (outside the score)")
798	    a("")
799	    a("A global caveat that shapes many PARTIAL scores: **time does not pass** in "
800	      "the simulation. Timers never count, so every documented behavior that "
801	      "depends on elapsed time (rollover interrupts, capture, WDT expiry, baud "
802	      "timing) is structurally absent.")
803	    a("")
804	    a("## Score")
805	    a("")
806	    a(f"**{pct:.1f}% compliant** — {tally[COMPLIANT]} of {total_scored} scored families.")
807	    a("")
808	    a("| Category | Families |")
809	    a("|---|---|")
810	    for s in SCORED:
811	        a(f"| {s} | {tally[s]} |")
812	    n_undoc = sum(1 for f, v in FINDINGS.items() if v.score == UNDOCUMENTED and f in fam_paths)
813	    n_frame = sum(1 for f, v in FINDINGS.items() if v.score == FRAMEWORK and f in fam_paths)
814	    a(f"| UNDOCUMENTED (outside score) | {n_undoc} |")
815	    a(f"| FRAMEWORK (outside score) | {n_frame} |")
816	    a("")
817	
818	    if stale:
819	        a("## ⚠ STALE findings (model changed since audit — review these entries)")
820	        a("")
821	        for s in stale:
822	            a(f"- probe `{s}` no longer reproduces")
823	        a("")
824	    if unscored:
825	        a("## ⚠ UNSCORED commands (added to msp430.py without an audit entry)")
826	        a("")
827	        for f in unscored:
828	            a(f"- `{f}`")
829	        a("")
830	
831	    a("## Findings by subsystem")
832	    for subsystem in sorted(by_subsystem):
833	        a("")
834	        a(f"### {subsystem}")
835	        a("")
836	        a("| Family | Score | Citation | Finding |")
837	        a("|---|---|---|---|")
838	        for fam, v in sorted(by_subsystem[subsystem]):
839	            n = len(fam_paths[fam])
840	            fam_disp = f"`{fam}`" + (f" ({n} paths)" if n > 1 else "")
841	            text = v.text.replace("|", "\\|")
842	            probe_note = f" *(probe: `{v.probe}`)*" if v.probe else ""
843	            a(f"| {fam_disp} | {v.score} | {v.citation} | {text}{probe_note} |")
844	
845	    a("")
846	    a("## MISSING — documented behavior with no corresponding command")
847	    a("")
848	    a("| Subsystem | Citation | Gap |")
849	    a("|---|---|---|")
850	    for m in MISSING:
851	        a(f"| {m.subsystem} | {m.citation} | {m.text} |")
852	    a("")
853	    a("## Unmodeled subsystems (not scored)")
854	    a("")
855	    a("The device model never claims these FR5994 modules; listed so their "
856	      "absence is a recorded decision rather than an oversight:")
857	    a("")
858	    for u in UNMODELED:
859	        a(f"- {u}")
860	    a("")
861	    a("## Appendix — every registered path and its family score")
862	    a("")
863	    a("| Path | Family | Score |")
864	    a("|---|---|---|")
865	    for fam in sorted(fam_paths):
866	        score = FINDINGS[fam].score if fam in FINDINGS else "UNSCORED"
867	        for path in fam_paths[fam]:
868	            a(f"| `{path}` | `{fam}` | {score} |")
869	    a("")
870	    return "\n".join(lines)
871	
872	
873	def main() -> int:
874	    """Run the audit and write the Markdown report."""
875	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
876	    parser.add_argument(
877	        "--output",
878	        default=str(REPO_ROOT / "docs" / "audits" / "msp430-compliance-report.md"),
879	        help="Report destination (default: docs/audits/msp430-compliance-report.md)",
880	    )
881	    args = parser.parse_args()
882	
883	    fam_paths, unscored, stale = run_audit()
884	    report = render_report(fam_paths, unscored, stale)
885	
886	    out = Path(args.output)
887	    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
888	    out.write_text(report)
889	
890	    print(f"report: {out}")
891	    print(f"families: {len(fam_paths)}  unscored: {len(unscored)}  stale probes: {len(stale)}")
892	    for f in unscored:
893	        print(f"  UNSCORED: {f}")
894	    for s in stale:
895	        print(f"  STALE: {s}")
896	    return 1 if (unscored or stale) else 0
897	
898	
899	if __name__ == "__main__":
900	    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""SCPI compliance audit for ``silmulator/devices/msp430.py``.

Scores every SCPI command family the simulated MSP430 implements against the
TI MSP430FR5994 documentation shipped in ``hardware_docs/ti/MSP430FR5994/``:

- SLAU367P  — MSP430FR58xx/59xx/6xx Family User's Guide
- SLASE54D  — MSP430FR599x datasheet

The audit is a curated findings database plus live behavioral probes.
Probes re-execute the questionable behavior against a fresh ``MSP430()``
instance every run, so the report stays honest as the device model evolves:

- a command added to msp430.py without an audit entry is reported UNSCORED;
- a finding whose probe no longer reproduces is reported STALE (the model
  changed; the audit entry needs review).

Usage:
    python scripts/audit_msp430.py [--output docs/audits/msp430-compliance-report.md]

Exit code is 0 when the audit itself ran cleanly (findings are data, not
failures); 1 when there are UNSCORED commands or STALE findings.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import re
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Callable, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT))

from silmulator.devices.msp430 import MSP430  # noqa: E402

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Scoring categories
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

COMPLIANT = "COMPLIANT"              # matches doc for typical use and boundaries
PARTIAL = "PARTIAL"                  # right concept, misses documented edge cases
NON_COMPLIANT = "NON_COMPLIANT"      # behavior contradicts the doc for typical use
ACCEPTS_INVALID = "ACCEPTS_INVALID"  # silently accepts states the doc says cannot exist
UNDOCUMENTED = "UNDOCUMENTED"        # simulator convenience with no doc basis
FRAMEWORK = "FRAMEWORK"              # IEEE-488.2/SCPI plumbing from BaseDevice, not TI-doc scoped

# Categories that count toward the compliance score. UNDOCUMENTED and
# FRAMEWORK sit outside it (decision recorded in the umbrella plan).
SCORED = (COMPLIANT, PARTIAL, NON_COMPLIANT, ACCEPTS_INVALID)

UG = "SLAU367P"
DS = "SLASE54D"


@dataclass
class Finding:
    """One audited command family."""

    subsystem: str
    score: str
    citation: str          # document + section, e.g. "SLAU367P §25.2.1.1"
    text: str              # what was checked and what was found
    probe: Optional[str] = None  # name of the probe that re-verifies this


@dataclass
class Missing:
    """Doc-described behavior with no corresponding command."""

    subsystem: str
    citation: str
    text: str


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Family normalization: collapse indexed paths (PORT3, CHANNEL7, TIMERA1, CC2)
# into one auditable family. Order matters: longer prefixes first.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

_FAMILY_SUBS = [
    (re.compile(r"\bPORT\d+"), "PORTn"),
    (re.compile(r"\bCHANNEL\d+"), "CHANNELn"),
    (re.compile(r"\bTIMERA\d+"), "TIMERAn"),
    (re.compile(r"\bTIMERB\d+"), "TIMERBn"),
    (re.compile(r"\bUART\d+"), "UARTn"),
    (re.compile(r"\bSPI\d+"), "SPIn"),
    (re.compile(r"\bI2C\d+"), "I2Cn"),
    (re.compile(r"\bCC\d+"), "CCn"),
    (re.compile(r"\bCH\d+"), "CHn"),
    (re.compile(r"\bTA\d+"), "TAn"),
    (re.compile(r"\bTB\d+"), "TBn"),
    (re.compile(r"\bP\d+"), "Pn"),
    (re.compile(r"\bA\d+"), "An"),
    (re.compile(r"\bB\d+"), "Bn"),
]


def family(path: str) -> str:
    """Collapse an indexed SCPI path into its command family."""
    out = path
    for rx, repl in _FAMILY_SUBS:
        out = rx.sub(repl, out)
    return out


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Probes — each re-verifies one recorded behavior against a fresh device.
# A probe returns True when the finding still reproduces.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _errors(dev: MSP430) -> int:
    """Number of queued SCPI errors on the device."""
    return len(dev._error_queue)


def probe_timer_divider_128(dev: MSP430) -> bool:
    """/128 is rejected — no ID×TAIDEX combination produces it (§25.2.1.1)."""
    dev.process("TIMERA0:CLOCK:DIVIDER 128")
    return _errors(dev) == 1 and dev.timer_a[0].clock_divider == 1


def probe_adc_ignores_reference(dev: MSP430) -> bool:
    """Raw conversion scales by the selected reference (SLAU367P §34.2.1 Eq. 13)."""
    dev.process("ADC:REFERENCE VREF")
    dev.inject_adc(0, 1.2)
    raw = int(dev.process("ADC:CHANNEL0:RAW?"))
    return raw == 4095  # 1.2 V vs 1.2-V VREF (REFVSEL reset default) is full scale


def probe_adc_convert_invalid_channel(dev: MSP430) -> bool:
    """Conversion on a nonexistent channel returns '0' instead of an error."""
    resp = dev.process("ADC:CONVERT 99")
    return resp == "0" and _errors(dev) == 0


def probe_adc_reference_unvalidated(dev: MSP430) -> bool:
    """Reference is validated against the fixed ADC12VRSEL/REF_A set."""
    dev.process("ADC:REFERENCE BANANA")
    return _errors(dev) == 1 and dev.adc[0].reference == "AVCC"  # rejected; default unchanged


def probe_adc_converts_without_enable(dev: MSP430) -> bool:
    """Conversion succeeds with the channel disabled (no ADC12ENC gate)."""
    dev.inject_adc(0, 1.0)
    raw = int(dev.process("ADC:CONVERT 0"))
    return raw > 0 and not dev.adc[0].enabled


def probe_adc_oversample_unvalidated(dev: MSP430) -> bool:
    """Oversample accepts arbitrary values (feature has no ADC12_B basis)."""
    dev.process("ADC:OVERSAMPLE 12345")
    return _errors(dev) == 0 and dev.adc[0].oversample == 12345


def probe_cpu_reg_20bit(dev: MSP430) -> bool:
    """CPUX registers are 20-bit; the model masks writes to 20 bits (0xFFFFF)."""
    dev.process("CPU:REGISTER 4,0x12345")
    return dev.process("CPU:REGISTER? 4") == "0x12345"


def probe_cpu_pc_validated(dev: MSP430) -> bool:
    """PC rejects odd and >20-bit values that cannot exist in hardware."""
    dev.process("CPU:PC 0x123457")
    odd_and_wide_rejected = _errors(dev) == 1 and dev._pc != 0x123457
    dev.process("CPU:PC 0x4000")
    even_in_range_accepted = _errors(dev) == 1 and dev._pc == 0x4000
    return odd_and_wide_rejected and even_in_range_accepted


def probe_cpu_reset_vector_pc(dev: MSP430) -> bool:
    """CPU:RESET fetches PC from the reset vector at 0xFFFE, defaulting to 0x4000."""
    dev.process("CPU:RESET")
    default_ok = dev._pc == 0x4000
    dev.process('MEMORY:WRITE 0xFFFE,0x00')
    dev.process('MEMORY:WRITE 0xFFFF,0xC0')
    dev.process("CPU:RESET")
    vector_ok = dev._pc == 0xC000
    return default_ok and vector_ok


def probe_dco_freq_continuous(dev: MSP430) -> bool:
    """DCO accepts arbitrary frequencies; hardware has discrete DCOFSEL steps."""
    dev.process("CLOCK:DCO:FREQUENCY 3141592")
    return _errors(dev) == 0 and dev.clock.dco_frequency == 3141592.0


def probe_lpm35_accepted(dev: MSP430) -> bool:
    """LPM3.5 and LPM4.5 both exist on FR5994 (SLAU367P §2.2.4) and are accepted."""
    dev.process("POWER:MODE LPM3.5")
    lpm35_ok = _errors(dev) == 0 and dev.pm.mode == "LPM3.5"
    dev.process("POWER:MODE LPM4.5")
    lpm45_ok = _errors(dev) == 0 and dev.pm.mode == "LPM4.5"
    return lpm35_ok and lpm45_ok


def probe_mclk_source_set(dev: MSP430) -> bool:
    """MCLK's source set matches CSCTL2.SELM: MODCLK accepted, REFO rejected."""
    dev.process("CLOCK:MCLK:SOURCE MODCLK")
    accepted_modclk = _errors(dev) == 0 and dev.clock.mclk_source == "MODCLK"
    dev.process("CLOCK:MCLK:SOURCE REFO")
    rejected_refo = _errors(dev) == 1
    return accepted_modclk and rejected_refo


def probe_mclk_divider_64(dev: MSP430) -> bool:
    """DIVM stops at /32 (SLAU367P §3.3.3 CSCTL3); /64 is rejected."""
    dev.process("CLOCK:MCLK:DIVIDER 64")
    return _errors(dev) == 1 and dev.clock.mclk_div == 1


def probe_smclk_source_unvalidated(dev: MSP430) -> bool:
    """SMCLK's source set matches MCLK's: MODCLK accepted, BANANA rejected."""
    dev.process("CLOCK:SMCLK:SOURCE MODCLK")
    accepted_modclk = _errors(dev) == 0 and dev.clock.smclk_source == "MODCLK"
    dev.process("CLOCK:SMCLK:SOURCE BANANA")
    rejected_banana = _errors(dev) == 1
    return accepted_modclk and rejected_banana


def probe_aclk_divider_unvalidated(dev: MSP430) -> bool:
    """ACLK divider matches DIVA's /1-/32 set (SLAU367P §3.3.3); /64 is rejected."""
    dev.process("CLOCK:ACLK:DIVIDER 64")
    return _errors(dev) == 1 and dev.clock.aclk_div == 1


def probe_mclk_freq_ignores_source(dev: MSP430) -> bool:
    """MCLK:FREQUENCY? follows the selected source: LFXT-sourced MCLK reads LFXT/div."""
    dev.process("CLOCK:MCLK:SOURCE LFXT")
    freq = float(dev.process("CLOCK:MCLK:FREQUENCY?"))
    return freq == dev.clock.lfxt_frequency / dev.clock.mclk_div


def probe_i2c_frequency_unvalidated(dev: MSP430) -> bool:
    """I2C clock accepts non-standard values (validation is dead code)."""
    dev.process("I2C0:FREQUENCY 12345")
    return _errors(dev) == 0 and dev.i2c[0].clock_frequency == 12345


def probe_i2c_transfer_ignores_address(dev: MSP430) -> bool:
    """I2C TRANSFER parses a target address, then never uses it."""
    r1 = dev.process('I2C0:TRANSFER 0x50,"AB"')
    dev.reset()
    r2 = dev.process('I2C0:TRANSFER 0x77,"AB"')
    return r1 == r2 == "00" and _errors(dev) == 0


def probe_i2c_write_always_acks(dev: MSP430) -> bool:
    """I2C WRITE returns ACK unconditionally; no NACK path exists."""
    return dev.process('I2C0:WRITE "DEADBEEF"') == "ACK"


def probe_wdt_stub(dev: MSP430) -> bool:
    """WDT state cannot change and a wrong password does not cause a PUC."""
    pc_before = dev._pc
    dev.process("WDT:PASSWORD 0x1234")  # wrong password: real part resets
    state = dev.process("WDT:STATE?")
    return state == "RUNNING" and _errors(dev) == 0 and dev._pc == pc_before


def probe_interrupt_stub(dev: MSP430) -> bool:
    """Interrupt system is a stub: vector is a constant, flags always 0."""
    return (
        dev.process("INTERRUPT:VECTOR?") == "0xFFFF"
        and dev.process("INTERRUPT:FLAG?") == "0"
    )


def probe_memory_unmapped(dev: MSP430) -> bool:
    """Reads of vacant/impossible addresses return 0x00 with no error."""
    resp = dev.process("MEMORY:READ 0x999999")
    return resp == "0x00" and _errors(dev) == 0


def probe_timer_count_over_16bit(dev: MSP430) -> bool:
    """Writes beyond TAxR's 16 bits are rejected with -222 (§25.2.1)."""
    dev.process("TIMERA0:COUNT 0x12345")
    return _errors(dev) == 1 and dev.timer_a[0].count <= 0xFFFF


def probe_timer_cc_capture_ignored(dev: MSP430) -> bool:
    """CC MODE stores the CAP bit: CAPTURE persists and reads back (§25.2.4)."""
    dev.process("TIMERA0:CC1:MODE CAPTURE")
    return dev.process("TIMERA0:CC1:MODE?") == "CAPTURE" and _errors(dev) == 0


def probe_gpio_pin_index_unvalidated(dev: MSP430) -> bool:
    """Pin numbers beyond 7 are rejected with -222 on an 8-bit port."""
    dev.process("GPIO:PORT1:PIN:VALUE 12,1")
    return _errors(dev) == 1 and dev.ports[1].output == 0


def probe_gpio_pull_both(dev: MSP430) -> bool:
    """Pull-up and pull-down are mutually exclusive on one pin (one PxREN bit)."""
    dev.process("GPIO:PORT1:PULLUP 0x01")
    dev.process("GPIO:PORT1:PULLDOWN 0x01")
    return dev.ports[1].pullup & dev.ports[1].pulldown & 0x01 == 0


def probe_gpio_input_ignores_pulls(dev: MSP430) -> bool:
    """Undriven input pins with REN enabled read PxOUT's pull level (§12.2.4)."""
    dev.process("GPIO:PORT1:DIRECTION 0x00")
    dev.process("GPIO:PORT1:RESISTOR:ENABLE 0xFF")
    dev.process("GPIO:PORT1:OUTPUT 0xFF")
    return dev.process("GPIO:PORT1:INPUT?") == "0xFF"


def probe_uart_send_while_disabled(dev: MSP430) -> bool:
    """UART SEND works with the module disabled (no UCSWRST gate)."""
    dev.process('UART0:SEND "HI"')
    return not dev.uart[0].enabled and bytes(dev.uart[0].tx_buffer) == b"HI"


def probe_spi_transfer_while_disabled(dev: MSP430) -> bool:
    """SPI TRANSFER works with the module disabled."""
    resp = dev.process('SPI0:TRANSFER "AA"')
    return resp == "00" and not dev.spi[0].enabled


PROBES: Dict[str, Callable[[MSP430], bool]] = {
    name[len("probe_"):]: fn
    for name, fn in sorted(globals().items())
    if name.startswith("probe_") and callable(fn)
}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Findings database — one entry per command family (see family()).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

F = Finding

FINDINGS: Dict[str, Finding] = {
    # --- IEEE-488.2 / SCPI framework (BaseDevice) --------------------------
    "*IDN": F("Framework", FRAMEWORK, "IEEE 488.2", "Identification string; TI docs do not define a SCPI surface for this part."),
    "*RST": F("Framework", FRAMEWORK, "IEEE 488.2; " + UG + " §1.2", "Restores simulator defaults. Diverges from a real PUC in the WDT finding (WDT unaffected)."),
    "*CLS": F("Framework", FRAMEWORK, "IEEE 488.2", "Clears error queue and event status register."),
    "*ESE": F("Framework", FRAMEWORK, "IEEE 488.2", "Event status enable register plumbing."),
    "*ESR": F("Framework", FRAMEWORK, "IEEE 488.2", "Event status register read-and-clear."),
    "*OPC": F("Framework", FRAMEWORK, "IEEE 488.2", "Operation-complete flag."),
    "*SRE": F("Framework", FRAMEWORK, "IEEE 488.2", "Service request enable register."),
    "*STB": F("Framework", FRAMEWORK, "IEEE 488.2", "Status byte composition."),
    "*TST": F("Framework", FRAMEWORK, "IEEE 488.2", "Self-test always passes."),
    "*WAI": F("Framework", FRAMEWORK, "IEEE 488.2", "No-op; simulation has no pending operations."),
    "SYSTEM:ERROR": F("Framework", FRAMEWORK, "SCPI-99 §21.8", "FIFO error queue."),
    "SYSTEM:ERROR:NEXT": F("Framework", FRAMEWORK, "SCPI-99 §21.8", "Alias of SYSTEM:ERROR."),
    "SYSTEM:ERROR:COUNT": F("Framework", FRAMEWORK, "SCPI-99 §21.8", "Error queue depth."),
    "SYSTEM:VERSION": F("Framework", FRAMEWORK, "SCPI-99 §21.21", "Reports SCPI version 1999.0."),

    # --- CPU ---------------------------------------------------------------
    "CPU:RESET": F("CPU", COMPLIANT, UG + " §1.2, §4.3.1",
                   "Reset fetches PC from the reset vector at 0xFFFE/0xFFFF (little-endian word), "
                   "defaulting to 0x4000 — FRAM code start (SLASE54D memory map) — when the vector "
                   "has not been written, matching a real BOR/POR/PUC.",
                   probe="cpu_reset_vector_pc"),
    "CPU:HALT": F("CPU", UNDOCUMENTED, "—", "Debug-style halt; the User's Guide models this via the EEM debug logic, not a device command."),
    "CPU:RUN": F("CPU", UNDOCUMENTED, "—", "Counterpart of CPU:HALT; simulator convenience."),
    "CPU:STATE": F("CPU", UNDOCUMENTED, "—", "RUNNING/HALTED/STOPPED status of the simulated core."),
    "CPU:PC": F("CPU", COMPLIANT, UG + " §4.3.1",
                "PC is a 20-bit register whose bit 0 is always 0. The model rejects odd values and "
                "values beyond 20 bits with -222, matching hardware's word-aligned addressing.",
                probe="cpu_pc_validated"),
    "CPU:REGISTER": F("CPU", COMPLIANT, UG + " §4.3",
                      "CPUX registers R0–R15 are 20-bit; writes are masked to 20 bits (0xFFFFF), "

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Audit engine
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def run_audit() -> Tuple[Dict[str, List[str]], List[str], List[str]]:
    """Map handler paths to families; run probes.

    Returns (family → concrete paths, unscored families, stale probe names).
    """
    dev = MSP430()
    fam_paths: Dict[str, List[str]] = {}
    for path in sorted(dev._handlers):
        fam_paths.setdefault(family(path), []).append(path)

    unscored = sorted(f for f in fam_paths if f not in FINDINGS)

    stale: List[str] = []
    for name, probe in PROBES.items():
        if not probe(MSP430()):
            stale.append(name)
    return fam_paths, unscored, stale


def render_report(fam_paths: Dict[str, List[str]], unscored: List[str],
                  stale: List[str]) -> str:
    """Render the Markdown compliance report."""
    scored = {f: v for f, v in FINDINGS.items() if v.score in SCORED and f in fam_paths}
    tally = {s: sum(1 for v in scored.values() if v.score == s) for s in SCORED}
    total_scored = sum(tally.values())
    pct = 100.0 * tally[COMPLIANT] / total_scored if total_scored else 0.0

    by_subsystem: Dict[str, List[Tuple[str, Finding]]] = {}
    for fam, finding in FINDINGS.items():
        if fam in fam_paths:
            by_subsystem.setdefault(finding.subsystem, []).append((fam, finding))

    lines: List[str] = []
    a = lines.append
    a("# MSP430 SCPI Compliance Report")
    a("")
    a("Audit of `silmulator/devices/msp430.py` against TI documentation.")
    a("")
    a("| Ground truth | Revision |")
    a("|---|---|")
    a("| MSP430FR58xx/59xx/6xx Family User's Guide | **SLAU367P** |")
    a("| MSP430FR599x datasheet | **SLASE54D** |")
    a("")
    a("Generated by `scripts/audit_msp430.py` — re-run it after changing "
      "`msp430.py`; probes verify each mechanical finding still reproduces.")
    a("")
    a("## Scope and method")
    a("")
    a("Every registered SCPI path is collapsed into a command family "
      f"({sum(len(p) for p in fam_paths.values())} paths → {len(fam_paths)} families) "
      "and each family is scored:")
    a("")
    a("- **COMPLIANT** — matches the doc for typical use and boundary values")
    a("- **PARTIAL** — right concept, misses documented edge cases or side effects")
    a("- **NON_COMPLIANT** — contradicts the doc for typical use")
    a("- **ACCEPTS_INVALID** — silently accepts states the doc says cannot exist "
      "(own category per the audit plan)")
    a("- **UNDOCUMENTED** — simulator convenience with no doc basis (outside the score)")
    a("- **FRAMEWORK** — IEEE-488.2/SCPI plumbing from `BaseDevice` (outside the score)")
    a("")
    a("A global caveat that shapes many PARTIAL scores: **time does not pass** in "
      "the simulation. Timers never count, so every documented behavior that "
      "depends on elapsed time (rollover interrupts, capture, WDT expiry, baud "
      "timing) is structurally absent.")
    a("")
    a("## Score")
    a("")
    a(f"**{pct:.1f}% compliant** — {tally[COMPLIANT]} of {total_scored} scored families.")
    a("")
    a("| Category | Families |")
    a("|---|---|")
    for s in SCORED:
        a(f"| {s} | {tally[s]} |")
    n_undoc = sum(1 for f, v in FINDINGS.items() if v.score == UNDOCUMENTED and f in fam_paths)
    n_frame = sum(1 for f, v in FINDINGS.items() if v.score == FRAMEWORK and f in fam_paths)
    a(f"| UNDOCUMENTED (outside score) | {n_undoc} |")
    a(f"| FRAMEWORK (outside score) | {n_frame} |")
    a("")

    if stale:
        a("## ⚠ STALE findings (model changed since audit — review these entries)")
        a("")
        for s in stale:
            a(f"- probe `{s}` no longer reproduces")
        a("")
    if unscored:
        a("## ⚠ UNSCORED commands (added to msp430.py without an audit entry)")
        a("")
        for f in unscored:
            a(f"- `{f}`")
        a("")

    a("## Findings by subsystem")
    for subsystem in sorted(by_subsystem):
        a("")
        a(f"### {subsystem}")
        a("")
        a("| Family | Score | Citation | Finding |")
        a("|---|---|---|---|")
        for fam, v in sorted(by_subsystem[subsystem]):
            n = len(fam_paths[fam])
            fam_disp = f"`{fam}`" + (f" ({n} paths)" if n > 1 else "")
            text = v.text.replace("|", "\\|")
            probe_note = f" *(probe: `{v.probe}`)*" if v.probe else ""
            a(f"| {fam_disp} | {v.score} | {v.citation} | {text}{probe_note} |")

    a("")
    a("## MISSING — documented behavior with no corresponding command")
    a("")
    a("| Subsystem | Citation | Gap |")
    a("|---|---|---|")
    for m in MISSING:
        a(f"| {m.subsystem} | {m.citation} | {m.text} |")
    a("")
    a("## Unmodeled subsystems (not scored)")
    a("")
    a("The device model never claims these FR5994 modules; listed so their "
      "absence is a recorded decision rather than an oversight:")
    a("")
    for u in UNMODELED:
        a(f"- {u}")
    a("")
    a("## Appendix — every registered path and its family score")
    a("")
    a("| Path | Family | Score |")
    a("|---|---|---|")
    for fam in sorted(fam_paths):
        score = FINDINGS[fam].score if fam in FINDINGS else "UNSCORED"
        for path in fam_paths[fam]:
            a(f"| `{path}` | `{fam}` | {score} |")
    a("")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def main() -> int:
    """Run the audit and write the Markdown report."""
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--output",
        default=str(REPO_ROOT / "docs" / "audits" / "msp430-compliance-report.md"),
        help="Report destination (default: docs/audits/msp430-compliance-report.md)",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args()

    fam_paths, unscored, stale = run_audit()
    report = render_report(fam_paths, unscored, stale)

    out = Path(args.output)
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out.write_text(report)

    print(f"report: {out}")
    print(f"families: {len(fam_paths)}  unscored: {len(unscored)}  stale probes: {len(stale)}")
    for f in unscored:
        print(f"  UNSCORED: {f}")
    for s in stale:
        print(f"  STALE: {s}")
    return 1 if (unscored or stale) else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
